main_text.p: tollitur una pullulans inde obligatio: fuit autem Materia illa quæ causam dedit juratione, radix ejus obligationis quæ ex illa juratione infecuta est. Juramentum enim 42. reg. Jur. in Sexto.{a} sequitur naturam & conditionem actus cui adjungitur, id est Materiæ circa quam versatur, sicut accessorium sequitur naturam sui principalis{b}: & quæ accessorium locum obtinent, inquiunt jurisconsulti, extinguuntur, cum principales res peremptæ fuerint.
main_text.head: SECT. VIII.
main_text.p: Casus 61Casus ultimus est, de solutione vinculi per Relaxationem Partis, ejus sc. cui juratum est: ut si Caius Titio aliquid promiserit, an remittente Titio obligationem, Caius promissi religione exolutus sit? Ubi imprimis observandum hunc loquendi modum Remittere Juramentum, & alium ei confimilem, Juramenti gratiam facere, apud bonos authores non uno semper sensu accipi. Summuntur enim interdum cum relatione ad juramentum præstandum, & sic is dicitur alteri remittere juramentum, vel juramenti gratiam facere, quicum alter ille paratus est jurare, contentus voluntate non postulat ab eo Juramentum, sed injurato credit, vel alia quacunque de
{b} b l 2. ff. de pecul. legat.

page.notes: Right margin shows only small edge marks; no printed text there. The left-margin note marked "a" is printed as "* 42. reg. Jur. in Sexto."; the note marked "b" is printed as "ᵇ l 2. ff. de pecul. legat." and the "l 2" reading is doubtful. "Cafus 61" is italic in the margin and read as Casus, since the long s is printed as f. The page opens mid-sentence, so the first paragraph is marked as continued. The heading "S E C T. VIII." is spaced capitals and is read as a division heading. Spelling of "Juramenti" and "juratione" follows the printed j, since j is a consonant here. Pages with "injurato" keep the printed j.
